title: Machine Guarding Checklist (29 CFR 1910.212)
subtitle: For on-site inspections of machines and their guards.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A, and note the machine or asset ID.
Report each Defect to the supervisor, keep the machine out of use while employees are exposed, and record the fix.
The manufacturer's instructions, machine-specific OSHA standards and site rules may add checks.

sections.title: Guarding methods and guard mounting
items: Point of operation, ingoing nip points, rotating parts and sources of flying chips or sparks are each covered by at least one guarding method.
Guarding also protects employees working near the machine, not just the operator.
Guard is fastened to the machine wherever attachment is possible; no loose or propped-up guards.
Where a guard cannot be fastened to the machine, it is firmly secured elsewhere and stays in position.
Guard has no feature that could injure someone, for example sharp edges, new pinch points or loose parts.

sections.title: Point of operation
items: The area where the machine actually works on the material is identified for this machine.
Where the machine's operation exposes an employee to injury, a guard or device protects the working area.
Guarding device conforms to any appropriate standard that applies to this machine type.
Where no specific standard applies, the operator cannot place any body part inside the danger zone at any point in the operating cycle.
Special hand tools let the operator place and remove material easily with hands kept out of the danger zone.
Required guarding stays in place when hand tools are used; the tools only supplement it.

Any guillotine cutters, shears, alligator shears, power presses, milling machines, power saws, jointers, portable power tools, forming rolls or calenders on site have been checked for point-of-operation guarding.

sections.title: Drums, fans and anchoring
items: Revolving drums, barrels and containers are enclosed by a guard.
With the enclosure open or removed, the drum, barrel or container cannot revolve; interlock tested.
Every fan whose blade periphery sits under 7 feet from the floor or working level has a guard.
No opening in the fan guard is larger than 1/2 inch, checked with a gauge or rule.
Machines designed for a fixed location are securely anchored and do not walk or move during operation.

references: 29 CFR 1910.212: General requirements for all machines (Part 1910 Subpart O: Machinery and Machine Guarding)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
